text:
maya: Heads up — bringing up kythera-14b (int4) canary. Seeing repeat OOMs on warmstart when batch_concurrency=4 and max_new_tokens default=512.

maya: Example trace: 
```
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory while allocating 1.2GiB (KV cache prefetch)
Stack: serving/runtime/kv_cache.cpp:423
```

samir: ugh. do we have a reproducer? warmstart pattern or coldstart?

maya: warmstart. heavy multi-turn prefixes (avg prompt len ~1200 tokens), so KV grows fast. repro on my local canary-2.

elena: main suspects: prefetch + high max_new_tokens + large microbatch. kw: fragmentation in the slot allocator.

ryan: try dropping generation.max_new_tokens to 256 as a quick safety. also try batch_concurrency=2. those two alone often avoid the OOM.

maya: did that: batch=2 + max_new=256 reduced OOMs but throughput drops 20% and latency CI shows tail increase.

samir: tradeoff expected. we should also try disabling prefetch for kythera; prefetch helps latency but spikes mem. set runtime.prefetch.enabled=false for canary.

elena: another knob: kv_trim_threshold and slot_compactor_reserve. current defaults: kv_trim_threshold=0.6, slot_compactor_reserve=0.02. I recommend testing kv_trim_threshold=0.5 and slot_compactor_reserve=0.05 for this model.

maya: patching canary with these config overrides now:
```
model_overrides {
  batch_concurrency: 2
  generation.max_new_tokens: 256
  runtime.prefetch.enabled: false
  runtime.kv_trim_threshold: 0.5
  runtime.slot_compactor_reserve: 0.05
}
```

deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: kythera-14b-int4 @ canary-2 at 6481240010 :rocket:

jana: quick note on quant: int4 build showed a small QA regression on summarization (ROUGE-L -0.6). We should compare int8 vs int4 quality before we change defaults. If int8 avoids OOMs we can prefer it until we tune int4.

ryan: good call. can we run a 1k-sample eval against baseline (fp16) and int8/int4? I can queue on eval-cluster.

maya: queued. i'll include prompts with long contexts to stress kv.

samir: also add a microbenchmark to capture token/sec and peak mem per request. include both warm and cold flows. use the new bench harness: https://internal.redwood/bench/kythera-compare (link)

elena: if int4 remains attractive performance-wise but unstable memory-wise, we can implement an automatic fallback: prefer int4, but if OOM observed >1% then route to int8 for that customer or route-level policy. very low friction to implement via model-routing rules.

maya: canary looks healthier so far with the new config, 6/10 warm requests still spike but not fatal. latency median +12ms, p95 +80ms. I'll keep it running and attach logs.

deploy-bot: Canary metrics (first 5m): alloc_peak_avg=10.8GiB, alloc_peak_p95=12.3GiB, OOM_rate=0.8%

jana: OOM_rate <1% is acceptable for a canary. For GA we target <0.1%.

ryan: once evals finish, if quality delta int4 vs fp16 > -1 ROUGE-L we should proceed with more aggressive frag fixes (free-list tuning + slot compactor GC) before GA.

maya: opening PR for default overrides and a short playbook: https://internal.redwood/pull/kythera-onboard-123 (will add config + rollback plan).

samir: thanks. next actions: (1) wait for evals (ryan), (2) run mem microbench (maya), (3) if int4 quality bad, switch default to int8 and continue int4 tuning (jana).

elena: also reminding — add a short note to model-catalog about the default max_new_tokens being 256 for kythera and rationale to prevent fragmentation OOMs. small docs prevent customers from hitting this blind.

maya: ack. will update model-catalog entry after GA decision. :thumbsup:

ryan: evals complete (quick summary): int8 ROUGE-L delta vs fp16 = -0.1, int4 = -0.7. Token/sec: int4 +18% vs int8, int8 +6% vs fp16.

jana: looks like int8 is a good compromise for GA. int4 can remain experimental with stricter routing.

maya: rolling kythera GA with int8 as default and keeping int4 canary with the conservative runtime settings. scheduling postmortem in two days to track fixes for int4 mem frag.

samir: nice. add the microbench graphs to the rollout notes.

elena: one last tip — enable kernel affinity tweak for int4 to lower temp alloc spikes: runtime.kernel_affinity=prefer-small-alloc. small wins.

maya: noted. thanks all.
